verdict.rationale: Adyen documents merchant-side integration paths for accepting agent traffic. With the Agentic Cart API, the merchant's server is called by Adyen so it does not need to integrate with each agent platform. The Feed API pushes catalog data to AI platforms, and there is a Google agentic commerce integration. Together these amount to a documented 'publish an endpoint/feed' route. However, nothing shows the path is self-serve, such as a dashboard toggle, an agreement to sign, or onboarding without sales involvement. missing for 10: evidence of a self-serve enablement step (setting/toggle or click-through agreement), documented onboarding/eligibility steps, independent or hands-on corroboration of merchant activation.

support.subject: As a merchant, I have a documented self-serve path to start accepting agent traffic — enable a setting, sign an agreement, or publish an endpoint

citations.quote: You accept payments from shoppers who use AI agents and want to expose your product catalog or checkout process to those agents.
Adyen communicates with your server so that you do not need to integrate with multiple agent platforms.
You upload product data in batches of up to 200 items.
Use this integration for processing Google Pay payments through Adyen, when Google agents (Google AI Mode or Gemini) initiate transactions with you.
